races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Unio Employee Benefits Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with winning course-and-distance form on good ground; T14 strike rate is live and a 19-day turnaround suits; OR=71 gives him a workable weight, and an uncontested lead is a significant tactical gift at this track.

runners_data.name: Altimara
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Ross O'Sullivan with decent recent course form at seven furlongs on good; needs a true gallop to deliver her best and a slow pace is a genuine concern, though T14 1/12 suggests yard in form.

runners_data.name: Naoi
runners_data.note: Lengthy absence of 402 days is a major flag; showed ability with three consecutive placed efforts but the layoff at 4yo is a significant unknown, even on a going that suits (3 of 4 placed on similar ground).

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan booked is a positive angle; has placed at seven furlongs on this going and won over six furlongs on good — the step back to seven and a prominent/hold-up style suits this controlled-pace scenario if he can get closer than his style suggests.

runners_data.name: La La Lucrative
runners_data.note: Three wins on good going and strong form figures, but genuinely a hold-up type that fades when not given a true pace — pushed into midfield on this map because of the overcrowded rear, and the slow tempo is an added concern for a horse who needs to be produced late.

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old who fades in the finish; zero wins from seven go-arounds on good ground is damning, the step up from five and six furlongs to seven is unproven, and blinkers on haven't changed the pattern.

runners_data.name: Free Solo
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, but displaced into the midfield map given the rear congestion; nine-year-old veteran who won on good at seven furlongs but the recent 5th of 9 over 8f on good was modest, and 48 days off adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Ballymagreehan
runners_data.note: Won over 8f at OR=62 but has been running in longer-trip company since; genuine hold-up horse squeezed forward on this map, and the drop back to 7f on good is better suited, though trainer shows 0/14 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: Consistent in its underperformance — five consecutive finishes outside the frame at 7f and 6f on varying ground; true rear-of-field horse represented in midfield here by necessity of map space, not natural role.

runners_data.name: Mr Perth
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a thin profile (4 runs) and no simulated good-ground wins in limited sample; his all-form finishes of 8-7-8-10 speak to a horse struggling at this level, and one good-ground run in his history undermines confidence.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: Consistent placer for Jessie Harrington (three 3rds in recent starts) with a clear liking for good ground at 7-8f; a natural hold-up horse displaced toward midfield by the packed rear — Shane Foley is a key booking and this horse does stay on, but needs pace to be produced.

runners_data.name: Kc Bear
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on a different surface but has placed twice on good at 7-8f; Nicola Burns (5) takes the ride and this is a genuine hold-up type forced into a midfield slot — the slow pace is its biggest enemy, as it needs horses to come back to it.

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win on good at 7f and placed at 8f on similar; OR=65 at 3yo with Rory Cleary aboard and good T14 figures — races in a role that suits this pace shape and is one of the most naturally positioned horses in the field.

runners_data.name: Hazrama
runners_data.note: Three runs in profile, all finished 10th or worse; hold-up runner tagged with a fading tendency, displaced into midfield here, and D.K. Weld is a trainer who can land a handicap but the form figures give little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Shamanka
runners_data.note: Dropping back significantly in trip to 7f having shown ability at 5-6f; natural hold-up horse mapped into midfield by rear congestion; trainer has no 14-day runners and 34 days since last run at a track/trip where past form doesn't persuade.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer with consistent mid-table finishes at 7-8f on good; Reese Holohan (7) claims aboard and the horse rarely wins but rarely finishes far back — the prominent style fits this race shape and he won't be far away.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran whose best form has been at six furlongs on faster ground; true hold-up type naturally settled near the rear but squeezed into midfield on the map — recent figures of 6-0-3-14-6 don't suggest a win is imminent.

runners_data.name: Oppenheimer
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly-raced hold-up runner with 4th on good at 7f as the best reference; Kevin Thomas Coleman's yard has been busy (T14 3/15) which is a positive; held up naturally so will be further back than ideal in this shape.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 7f on good in the last five runs and the form line isn't hopeless; a natural hold-up horse bumped into midfield on this map — no jockey listed is a minor concern, and recent efforts suggest a place at best rather than a win.

runners_data.name: Ninth Crusade
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 74 but all recent form has been over 5-6f on different ground; one good-ground run from six attempts is a real flag, the step up in trip is unproven, and no jockey listed alongside a tongue-tie raises questions.

runners_data.name: Sporting Hero
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who won over 5f on good and is now tackling 7f on a long 86-day break; the step up two furlongs is significant, the layoff is a risk, but William Durkan's yard struck at T14 and this horse does race prominently — the right style for this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and faces zero genuine pace pressure from another natural leader, meaning Adam Browne-Souza can dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo on good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown. Zheleznaya Dama and Sporting Hero will press forward to prominent positions just off the leader, creating a small front cluster but not a true pace duel — the gallop will be honest rather than scorching over seven furlongs. The bulk of this field is made up of hold-up types, but so many genuine closers — La La Lucrative, Kc Bear, Bear Right, Free Solo, Ballymagreehan, Hazrama and others — cannot all find their natural rear-of-field position in a 21-runner handicap, and several will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal. This race shape — one leader, modest pace, prominent cluster — strongly favours horses who travel prominently with cover and finish off a well-judged gallop, rather than closers who depend on a truly strong pace to create momentum from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Dictates, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh sets a controlled pace unchallenged and the race is truly run to suit those racing just off the leader.
scenarios.body: Faoladh tows the field along at an even, sustainable clip and those sitting second or third on his quarters get the perfect slingshot into the Leopardstown straight; with no late acceleration from deep, the prominent racers hold the advantage into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Faoladh Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace suits Faoladh himself and he proves good enough to steal a march turning for home at a moderate gallop.
scenarios.body: Faoladh has winning course form over seven furlongs on this going and with a featherlight pace load set by himself, he may never be headed if the prominent chasers are slow to react; the field's hold-up runners will be finishing late into beaten horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Zheleznaya Dama or Sporting Hero push the early pace faster than expected, creating enough of a true gallop for hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace would string the field out and give the genuine closers — Rappell, Bear Right and Altimara — a shot at picking up tired rivals in the final two furlongs; however, with so many redistributed hold-up types forced wide and forward, the true late finishers are disadvantaged from the outset.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Wide Draw Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 21-runner field splits into two groups early, with those drawn wide unable to cross and racing in isolation.
scenarios.body: A divided field over seven furlongs on a flat track can produce two separate races, benefiting any horse in the larger or better-positioned group regardless of style; this is a low-probability shape but the sheer size of the field makes it a real tail risk.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh jumping cleanly and uncontested to the lead is the race-defining moment — if he secures his lead without being rushed, the prominent horses tracking him are immediately handed a major advantage over the large hold-up pack.

With 21 runners and a disproportionate number of natural hold-up types forced wide and forward in early stages, watch for crowding and interference on the first bend — horses like Bear Right, Kc Bear and La La Lucrative could be caught in traffic before settling.

Sporting Hero's 86-day absence is the key unknown for the prominent group — if he comes fresh and travels well to the lead, he changes the pace dynamic and stretches the field; if he is ring-rusty, the pace remains slow and Faoladh controls everything.

Zheleznaya Dama's positioning in the early stages is worth noting — as the most naturally prominent filly behind Faoladh, Rory Cleary will want to be second or third and covered; if she gets that slot, her 7f good-ground win reads as directly relevant form.

Naoi's 402-day layoff makes her a live market watch — if she shortens late despite the absence, it signals a trainer confident in the horse's wellbeing, and she does have the profile (multiple 3rds on similar ground) to run into a place fresh.

races.name: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Irish EBF Vinnie Roe Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Abbotsford
runners_data.note: Improving 3yo for D K Weld stepping markedly up in trip to 1m6f for the first time — the extra distance could be a leap of faith, though his sole win came over 1m2f on similar good ground and prominent style suits the expected shape; just 22 days since last run keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Cannes
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's pace-maker in this race shape, winning over 1m2f on good ground and twice placed at 1m2f-1m4f — faces a distance step-up himself but his role as sole front-runner gives him every chance of lasting longer than his rating suggests if granted a soft lead.

runners_data.name: Highwayman
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for O'Brien with a notable tendency to fade in the finish — his lone win was over 1m2f on good ground 38 days ago but the stamina for 1m6f combined with that finishing quirk makes him a hard horse to trust even if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's progressive type has won back-to-back, most recently over 1m3f on soft, and his prominent style aligns perfectly with the dominant race shape — Gary Carroll can track Cannes from the front and pounce, though the trainer's quiet 14-day strike rate (0/17) is a mild flag.

runners_data.name: Piazza San Marco
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's highest-rated runner here at OR 105 returns after 298 days off, last seen finishing sixth over 1m on heavy — the lengthy absence and form string showing no placing on good ground at this trip demands caution despite the class.

runners_data.name: Trojan Fighter
runners_data.note: Twomey's hold-up type comes here wearing a tongue-tie off 61 days' rest, having won over 1m3f on good ground but more recently beaten into eighth over that trip on soft — needs a pace collapse he is unlikely to get from a single modest front-runner.

runners_data.name: Wyman
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a horse in cracking form, winning consecutive races over 1m2f-1m3f on good ground with the tongue-piece — the step to 1m6f is the key unknown but Mrs Harrington's record of placing horses at the right time and the prominent style suit the shape.

runners_data.name: Keepsgettingbetter
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's lightly-weighted 128lb runner is by nature a hold-up horse, having placed five times from the rear, but the preponderance of genuine closers in this field means it is likely to end up closer to the pace than it wants — that compromised position weakens its chance.

runners_data.name: Teologia
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins including over 1m3f on good ground stamp her as a genuine contender, Ben Coen provides in-form jockey confidence, and the prominent headgear (p) fits the expected race shape — O'Brien's three-runner team here adds a tactical dimension but Teologia looks their sharpest stayer.

races.paceDynamic: Cannes is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate an honest but controllable gallop over 1m6f on good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown. Behind him, Abbotsford, Madbadanddangerous, Wyman, and Teologia all want prominent positions, creating a congested mid-pack battle for the first three spots from the outset, with the real danger of interference or traffic issues between the 2f and 3f-out markers as those four jostle for berths. Highwayman, Piazza San Marco, and Trojan Fighter will be further back, reliant on the prominent group burning themselves out, while Keepsgettingbetter — a true hold-up type — is redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear in this shape, meaning its natural deep position is unlikely to be available. The race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield profile: a sustainable but genuine pace from Cannes sets the table for a progressive prominent racer to sweep past in the straight, with any horse forced to make up significant ground from the rear facing a stern task on a track that does not dramatically disadvantage leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cannes Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cannes leads comfortably at a fair clip and the prominent quartet settle just behind him without incident.
scenarios.body: Cannes sets an even, honest gallop that stretches the field through the final mile without burning out the chasers, and the prominent runners—Madbadanddangerous, Wyman, or Teologia—are best placed to accelerate past him in the final 2f after sitting within two lengths throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent horses clash early and create a messy, uneven tempo with surges and checks through the first half-mile.
scenarios.body: The disruption shreds the rhythm of those prominent types who are compromised, handing an advantage to any hold-up runner that finds a clear passage — Highwayman or Trojan Fighter could pick off a tiring leader in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Cannes Lasts Under Light Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Cannes is gifted a soft lead and the prominent horses fail to mount a serious challenge until too late.
scenarios.body: With no early pressure from behind, Cannes dictates the fractions entirely on his own terms and the prominent runners find themselves unable to close the gap after he quickens slightly entering the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly strong enough to set up a deep closing run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Highwayman, Piazza San Marco, or Trojan Fighter would need the prominent quartet to push the gallop far harder than one front-runner naturally would, a scenario discounted because Cannes faces minimal pressure and Keepsgettingbetter is unlikely to secure its deepest position.

watchPoints.text: Abbotsford, Madbadanddangerous, Wyman, and Teologia will all attempt to fill the first three prominent slots — watch for pushing, checking, and interference between the 6f and 4f markers as four horses fight for two positions.

Cannes has won over 1m2f but has never raced beyond that distance — a step to 1m6f means his ability to see out the full trip is unproven and he may stop quickly entering the straight if the prominent runners press at the 3f pole.

Piazza San Marco returns from 298 days off without a prep run — even with Aidan O'Brien's resources, market moves at the off will be critical to gauge whether connections genuinely believe he is ready to fire first time back.

Keepsgettingbetter is the field's lowest weight at 128lbs but its true deep hold-up style means it will likely race closer to the pace than it wants — a position change from the stalls to the first bend will signal whether it finds its natural ground or is crowded forward.

Highwayman is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — watch his position at the 2f pole; if he has not improved by then, his chance is gone, and the trend may expose Trojan Fighter as the more reliable O'Brien hold-up runner.

races.name: Money Back Daily Specials With Tote.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Satono Chevalier
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Seamie Heffernan takes the mount for Flannery and on Good to Firm ground over this trip the horse can control fractions entirely — eight-year-old with a win at 13f on Good, proven in the conditions, and the race hinges largely on whether it can hold on.|

runners_data.name: Sea Coral
runners_data.note: Trained by Mrs Harrington with a strong recent 2/31 record in the past fortnight; fitted with a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, genuine hold-up horse who appreciated 13f on Good last time out in a placed effort, and the 8-day turnaround for a yard in form is a positive flag.|

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: 108 days off the track is the obvious concern, and the horse's best form has come at 16f-18f, making this 13f trip a shade sharp; prominent-style runner for the same Flannery yard as the leader, likely to be pushed up to track Satono Chevalier, and may offer a market clue if well-backed fresh.|

runners_data.name: Pavilion End
runners_data.note: Placed at 10f and 14f on Good this term, suggesting the horse handles both pace scenarios; a natural hold-up type for O'Brien whose recent form over this trip (2nd at 14f on Good) reads well, and Declan McDonogh is a strong booking at this venue.|

runners_data.name: Ben Hur
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Soft and placed at 16f on Good, so the step back to 13f here is the key question — Meade's four-year-old has a hold-up style and may find this trip just too short if the pace is moderate; the 22-day break is unexceptional but the form line at this trip looks thin.|

runners_data.name: Darius Dark
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins at 12f on Good earlier this campaign make the class and current form the strongest in the field; flagged as fading in the finish which is the caveat, and Coen takes the ride for Murtagh who has shown recent form (2/30), but the drop to OR=82 off a hat-trick suggests the handicapper may be catching up.|

runners_data.name: Celtic Druid
runners_data.note: Strong placed record at 12f-13f on Good and a winner on Standside, but the true hold-up profile means McCourt's five-year-old is unlikely to get far enough back in this pace shape to deliver a clean finish; best when able to close into a true run race, conditions here may frustrate.|

runners_data.name: Harry's Legacy
runners_data.note: The tongue-tie is already applied and the horse has shown it can place at 14f-17f on Good, but three consecutive out-of-the-places efforts including a 19th last time suggest confidence in its current form is limited; a natural hold-up operator who will struggle to find its rhythm when pushed into midfield by the race shape.|

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Won at 13f on Good earlier in the season so the course, distance and going are all confirmed positives; the headgear (blinkers-permitted) may sharpen it, but as a natural closer that is likely to find itself in the wrong part of the race given the pace dynamics, the Rogers runner faces a tactical headache.|

runners_data.name: Party Dress
runners_data.note: McCreery has placed two from 19 recently and the mare has some placed form at 14f-15f on Good; a hold-up type by nature that is being pushed into a midfield position by the density of closers in this field, and the 0-in-10 record on this going band at a realistic level is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Gaelic Drills
runners_data.note: Bolger's three-year-old is the rawest horse in the field with a form string of 54795 and no win or place from five starts; mapped prominent and likely to track the leader, but the horse has shown no ability to sustain its effort and the step up in trip to 13f looks ambitious.|

runners_data.name: Lauderdale King
runners_data.note: The trainer-jockey combination of Andrew Slattery is unusual and the 69-day absence is the longest in the field; flagged as fading in the finish, a natural hold-up horse redistributed forward on the map, and the best form has been in shorter 8f-10f races rather than at this 13f trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Satono Chevalier is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m5f handicap and, with no credible rivals willing to race alongside from the front, should establish an uncontested, controlled lead on Good to Firm ground at Leopardstown. Gaelic Drills and Ehteyat are mapped prominent but neither has the early-pace profile to seriously pressure Satono Chevalier, meaning the sectionals are likely to be honest but not genuinely searching — a rhythm that keeps the leader fresh into the straight. The bulk of this field is composed of hold-up types, yet the pace map cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; Celtic Druid, Harry's Legacy, Cooley's Mist, Party Dress and Lauderdale King are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the field simply carries too many closers to allow everyone their natural position. This race shape — one unhurried leader, a compressed mid-division of genuine hold-up horses unable to get far enough back — strongly favours horses that can race prominently or in a handy tracking position and sustain their effort through the straight, rather than those dependent on a strong late gallop to pick off rivals.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chevalier Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Satono Chevalier leads unchallenged and the pace is just honest enough to suit front-to-finish.
scenarios.body: Satono Chevalier bowls along at a fair clip on the Good to Firm surface, makes every yard and, with no rival able to close the gap through the final two furlongs, holds on grimly; horses that track closely and sustain pressure through the straight are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Runs Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Satono Chevalier is marginally too strong and a close-tracking prominent horse reels it in late.
scenarios.body: A runner settled just behind the leader in second or third gear picks up the pieces when Satono Chevalier begins to tie up inside the final furlong; Darius Dark, despite the fade flag, has the class and recent winning form to deliver from this position if the fractions suit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Field, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough to compress the field and several midfield horses finish in a heap.
scenarios.body: With true hold-up horses redistributed forward and unable to get far enough back, the race bunches and a wall of horses hits the line together; those with the best current form and ability to find a gap — Ben Hur and Pavilion End — are best placed from this cluster.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and genuine hold-up runners produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires horses like Celtic Druid, Harry's Legacy or Cooley's Mist to produce their natural hold-up race, but all are redistributed forward on the map and are unlikely to be far enough back to deliver a clean late sweep; the shape must collapse significantly for this to unfold.

watchPoints.text: Watch Satono Chevalier's early stride pattern — if Seamie Heffernan is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a genuine but controlled pace, the race may be over as a contest before the home turn and every other runner's chance deteriorates sharply.

Darius Dark's fade flag is critical in a race where the winner is likely to be set a proper test at 13f on Good to Firm — if Ben Coen is unable to hold the colt up and switch off in the early stages, the three-win form may be misleading about finishing ability.

The cluster of five hold-up horses (Celtic Druid, Harry's Legacy, Cooley's Mist, Party Dress, Lauderdale King) are all likely to race closer than their natural style dictates — watch for interference and traffic issues in the home straight as they find themselves hemmed in by their own tactical compromise.

Ehteyat's 108-day absence for Flannery makes it a notable market mover to track — if it is well supported from its morning price, the yard (which also trains the leader) may have deliberately placed it here fresh believing it is fit enough to track their own front-runner home.

Sea Coral's 8-day turnaround under Shane Foley for the Harrington yard, which has gone 2/31 in the last fortnight, is the sharpest form/trainer combination in the field for a hold-up horse — watch whether it gets a clear run two furlongs out.

races.name: Dublin To Bahrain Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Pink Oxalis
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with placed form at this course and trip; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim could help offset a wide draw, and good-to-firm going suits her based on a placed effort at Leopardstown over 8f on similar ground — needs a strong pace to deliver her late run.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners this five-year-old who wears a tongue-strap and has solid placed form over 7-8f on good ground; her hold-up style means she needs the race to be truly run to get herself into contention, and ten of her last 15 starts came on similar going.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old trained by Grassick who won over 7f on good and placed over 6f on good; the prominent style is perfectly suited to this uncontested-pace scenario and the step back to a mile from a strong flat track looks straightforward.

runners_data.name: Duchess Of Kenli
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old has only two starts but landed her maiden over 8f on good at the Curragh, giving her obvious claims at this trip; Declan McDonogh takes over and the prominent style means she can sit just behind the pacesetter without burning energy — limited form is the key caveat.

runners_data.name: Thrifty Of Digby
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner ridden by Shane Foley, with winning form over 8f and 10f on good ground; Mrs Harrington's mare wears a hood and will control the tempo entirely — her chance hinges on whether the pace she sets is too leisurely to hold off the pressing pack.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: K J Condon's five-year-old is a true hold-up horse at heart — her best form has come from off a genuine pace over 10-12f — and running over a flat mile out of her comfort zone stylistically, having been placed into midfield due to rear overcrowding; the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.91 tempers expectations despite tidy recent form.

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a mare who has won twice recently at 8-9f on good ground and is in fine form; she is naturally a hold-up type forced to operate from midfield given the rear of the field is congested, and the 0.92 STYLE_FIT flag is worth noting — watch how she travels once the pace settles.

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: D K Weld's tongue-tied gelding wears cheekpieces and has placed form at 9f on good, but prominent racing style has yielded only moderate returns at this level recently; Chris Hayes has experience of him but the form string suggests he has been finding these handicaps tough.

races.paceDynamic: Thrifty Of Digby is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push her, is set to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop over this flat Leopardstown mile on good-to-firm ground. Glory To Be and Duchess Of Kenli will press from prominent positions just off the leader, giving the race a competitive front section without turning it into a burn-up. The going report confirms consistent good-to-firm conditions all evening, which will keep the pace honest enough to reward those travelling smoothly just off the speed — prominent-to-midfield types are positioned to pounce at the two-furlong pole. This shape squarely favours the prominent and early-pressing profile; Marmeladova and Bella Colombia are genuine hold-up horses who are mapped into midfield only because the rear of the field is oversubscribed, and their redistribution means their true closing kick may arrive from further forward than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thrifty Controls, Pressers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Thrifty Of Digby settles into a comfortable solo lead and the early tempo is even enough for prominent runners to travel smoothly in behind.
scenarios.body: Thrifty sets an uncontested, metronomic gallop and the race develops into a straight sprint home, where Glory To Be and Duchess Of Kenli — travelling prominently throughout — are best placed to pounce; their ability to race close to the pace without expending extra energy in a tracking role gives them a decisive positional edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to string the field out and genuine closers get a clear run up the straight to deliver a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Pink Oxalis and Mallavelly, both authentic hold-up operators who have shown solid form on this ground type, would benefit most if the tempo ensures the front group ties itself up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Thrifty Of Digby Wins It
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is controlled and genuinely sub-par, allowing Thrifty to steal enough of a break turning in that rivals can never quite close her down.
scenarios.body: Thrifty Of Digby has winning form over both this distance and going, and a solo lead with no pressure is precisely the scenario that plays to a front-runner's strengths; a slow-burn pace would expose the inability of hold-up horses — mapped out of role — to produce a telling late burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If something unexpected quickens the tempo dramatically mid-race, causing the field to bunch and a scrambling finish to unfold.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish would randomise the result and could see any of Bella Colombia or Marmeladova — racing slightly out of their natural role — benefit from a messy sprint if they happen to be well placed at the moment the race fractures.

watchPoints.text: Duchess Of Kenli is unproven beyond two starts — if she travels sweetly for Declan McDonogh in the prominent position, her unexposed profile over 8f on this ground makes her a serious danger to the more exposed runners.

Bella Colombia and Marmeladova are both racing out of their natural hold-up role; watch at the start whether either drifts toward the rear instinctively, which would leave them with an impossible task from the back in a controlled-pace race.

Thrifty Of Digby's hood and front-running style will set the entire shape of this race — if Shane Foley allows her to steal a soft lead into the straight, the race may already be won before rivals realise it.

The going report confirms good-to-firm all evening at Leopardstown; any horse whose form profile shows a meaningful advantage on fast ground over this trip — notably Glory To Be and Duchess Of Kenli — gets an additional edge on this surface.

Pink Oxalis has placed form specifically on soft and standard-to-fast at Leopardstown over 8f; if the pace is strong enough to suit her late run, the 3lb claim from Jack Kearney could make her competitive weight despite a higher finishing position being required than her recent run of form suggests.
